I’m starting with `README.md` and the mandated wake-visual inspection skill, then I’ll audit the current rollout evidence before touching the controller. I’ll keep the work confined to this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf or neighboring/history sources.

The visual-signals skill applies because both sampled policies have wake keyframe sheets. It requires comparing the successful run with the informative domain-exit failure and cross-checking the images against metrics/diagnostics before any policy edit; I’m following that sequence now.

The numerical evidence separates three failure modes sharply: the seed was energetic but target-blind and exited after moving mostly downward; the low-effort positive-steering descendant was simply advected out in 16.7 time units; and the prefilled negative-steering/heading-rate candidate became unstable in 4.45 time units with force and moment RMS exploding by roughly three orders of magnitude. The positive-steering energy-regulated policy is the only success, reaching the target in 130.2 time units. I’m now checking whether the keyframes support that causal reading.

The keyframes confirm that the successful controller is genuinely self-propelled upstream into the developed wake, but it takes a wide S-shaped detour: its maximum lateral target offset is `5.425L` before it returns to the `0.75L` capture circle. That makes route damping—not more drive or a sign reversal—the evidence-backed improvement axis. I’m checking the observation conventions now so the damping term stays normalized, bounded, and within the public policy contract.

The skill’s required pre-edit diagnosis is complete. I’m recording one falsifiable candidate hypothesis now: preserve the only demonstrated successful gait and curvature sign, and add a small bounded damping term from the windowed target-bearing rate to reduce the wide lateral overshoot without weakening upstream propulsion.

The single candidate is now implemented, and the durable guidance has been materially revised with the key reusable lesson: the inherited right-exit cluster was confounded by under-driving, because a propulsively stronger controller with the same steering sign is the only demonstrated success. I’ve kept the new rate damping bounded and isolated from the successful gait parameters. Next I’m validating the schema and invoking the prescribed check runner.
